issues_confirmed.what: resolveCollision separates an overlapping pair by exactly `overlap = minDist - dist`, leaving them at exactly minDist; the merge test one pass later is a strict `dist < minDist`, so it is false. With dx exactly 0 (nx = 0, x never changes, no rounding slop) the test misses every frame forever. dx is exactly 0 for every drop from the Drop Fruit button because dropFruit always uses the same clamped fruitDropX and a dx==0 collision imparts no vx.
issues_confirmed.evidence: Replicated Fruits.ts + the draw() body headlessly. Two Cherries at identical x: 0 merges over 600 frames, 502 frames sitting at exactly-touching. Two Watermelons at identical x: 0 merges, 508 near-misses. Same two Cherries with a 5px x-offset: merges to Strawberry.

issues_confirmed.what: Both indices are added to mergedIndices unconditionally, but `if (nextIndex < fruitTypes.length)` pushes no replacement for the top tier, so two merging Watermelons both delete themselves.
issues_confirmed.evidence: Simulated two Watermelons with a 12px x-offset: board ends empty, 1 pair vanished with no replacement.

issues_confirmed.what: handleCanvasClick reads getBoundingClientRect() off `e.target`, which is the viewport-sized overlay, not the canvas. The canvas is w-[90vw] max-w-[800px] centred in a p-4 flex box (GameCanvas.tsx:126-127), so at 1280px wide drops land ~240px right of the cursor and saturate on the clamp at GameCanvas.tsx:24. The `as HTMLCanvasElement` cast hides it from TypeScript because e.target is typed EventTarget.

issues_confirmed.where: src/app/projects/DevilSuika/GameCanvas.tsx:114 and cleanup at 119-122, effect deps [mouseX] at :123
issues_confirmed.what: draw() re-arms itself with requestAnimationFrame but the id is never captured and cleanup never calls cancelAnimationFrame. The effect is keyed on mouseX. The overlay currently blocks mousemove from ever reaching the canvas listener (:58), so mouseX stays null and the effect never re-runs — that is the only thing keeping this to one loop. Letting mousemove through spawns a new self-perpetuating loop per mouse move over the same fruitsRef.
The translucent preview fruit is gated on `mouseX !== null`, which never becomes true because the overlay swallows mousemove. Nothing ever shows where a fruit will land.
dt is used raw. rAF pauses in a background tab, so the first frame back carries a multi-second dt.
issues_confirmed.evidence: One frame with dt = 3.0s teleports a Cherry from y=50 to the floor (y=788) and launches it back up at vy=-600 — it gains energy and tunnels through anything between.

issues_confirmed.what: The `dist !== 0` guard makes resolveCollision a no-op for two fruits at the identical point. Verified directly. Merged fruits spawn at the exact midpoint (GameCanvas.tsx:101), so two simultaneous merges at one spot reach it.
